cards.text: Jeremiah the prophet is in Jerusalem, writing a letter. It's going to the exiles Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, carried off from Jerusalem to Babylon. That's the surviving elders, the priests, the prophets and everyone else.

cards.question: Before Jeremiah's letter, Jeconiah, king of Judah, had already been carried off from Jerusalem too.

cards.text: No mail carrier runs to Babylon, friend, so this letter catches a ride. Two men are headed to King Nebuchadnezzar: Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah.

cards.question: Elasah and Gemariah are carrying Jeremiah's letter to Babylon. Who sent them to King Nebuchadnezzar?
Jeremiah's letter to the exiles opens by saying whose words these are. Whose are they?

cards.text: So it's the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, speaking to every exile in Babylon. If I'm one of them, I'm reading this letter with my bags ALREADY packed.

cards.question: The exiles are far from home in Babylon. What's the first thing the LORD tells them to do?

answers.text: Pack up and get ready to leave

cards.text: Build houses, settle down, plant gardens and eat their produce. Friend, that's not "hang tight," that's "CHANGE YOUR MAILING ADDRESS."

cards.question: The LORD tells the exiles to hold off on weddings and children until they're back home.

cards.text: Marry, have kids, and marry off those kids so they have kids too: "Multiply there; do not decrease." Then the LORD turns to the city they're living in.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell the exiles to seek for the city He sent them to?
The LORD also tells the exiles to pray to Him for that city. Why?

answers.text: If it prospers they will too
So its king will set them free
So its people will join them

cards.text: Pray for the city you didn't pick, friend. I spent years in a junk drawer, and I'll be honest: I never ONCE prayed for the drawer.
Then the letter turns to the prophets and diviners right there among the exiles. People have been drawing dreams out of them.

cards.question: The LORD tells the exiles to listen closely to the dreams they get from those prophets and diviners.
The prophets among the exiles are prophesying in the LORD's name. What does the LORD say about them?

answers.text: He sent them to test His people
They will be proven right later

cards.text: They use His name, and He never sent them. That's like somebody signing YOUR name on a card you never even saw.

cards.question: Then the LORD tells the exiles how long Babylon gets: "When Babylon’s ___ years are complete, I will attend to you…"

cards.text: Seventy years… okay, I'm gonna need a BIGGER calendar. When they're complete, the LORD will confirm His promise to restore the exiles to this place.

cards.question: The LORD says He knows the plans He has for the exiles. What are those plans meant to do?

answers.text: Prosper them and not harm them
Keep them in Babylon for good

cards.text: "For I know the plans I have for you, declares the LORD, plans to prosper you and not to harm you, to give you a future and a hope." A future AND a hope, friend, in a letter mailed to people in exile.

cards.question: When the exiles call upon the LORD and come and pray to Him, what does He say He'll do?
The LORD says the exiles will seek Him and find Him. When will they find Him?

answers.text: When they search with all their heart
When they get back to Jerusalem
When a new prophet shows up

cards.text: Then the LORD says, "I will be found by you…" Friend, I know a little something about getting found: just ask the dust in that junk drawer.

cards.question: The LORD promises to gather the exiles from all the nations and places He banished them to, and bring them back to the place He sent them from.

cards.text: And that's where we'll set this letter down for now. Don't go anywhere, friend, because Jeremiah's not done writing.

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 5 quotes "When Babylon's ___ years are complete, I will attend to you", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: "No mail carrier runs to Babylon, friend, so this letter catches a ride" gives a reason the letter went with Elasah and Gemariah. Jeremiah 29:3 only says the letter was entrusted to them. It never says why.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Jeremiah the prophet" is arguable. Jeremiah 29:1 says Jeremiah sent the letter, and verse 3 says he entrusted it to these two men. A baker could argue that Jeremiah sent them. Only the trip to King Nebuchadnezzar belongs to Zedekiah.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The right answer is shaped differently from the wrong answers, so it stands out. It starts with "If it prospers…" and both wrong answers start with "So its…".

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: This card only repeats the prayer-for-the-city point that cards 11 and 12 already covered, with a joke added. It tells no new part of the passage, so it is a recap card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: Five of the seven choice cards are multiple choice, two are true or false, and none are fill in the blank. Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: This card only repeats the answer to card 3 (He never sent them), with a joke added. It moves no part of the passage forward. The "falsely prophesying" detail in Jeremiah 29:9 is still never told.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the number "seventy" in a line they haven't seen. Nothing on the earlier cards lets them reason it out, so the card tests wording, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This card says the LORD will confirm His promise to restore the exiles to this place. That gives away the answer to card 12 (true or false: He will bring them back to the place He sent them from). It also rules out the card 7 wrong answer "Keep them in Babylon for good."

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Card 6 has just said the LORD will restore the exiles, so the setup rules out the wrong answer "Keep them in Babylon for good."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke flips the core action. In Jeremiah 29:14 the exiles find the LORD, but in the joke Papa Dorin is the one who gets found. "Just ask the dust in that junk drawer" also doesn't click right away, since the dust has no clear part in him being found.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.
